headline: Willem II: new coach, narrow favourites at home
summary: Willem II are bottom of the Eredivisie on 2 points, and they meet Cambuur with a new man in charge: John Stegeman was sacked and Adrie Koster is interim coach. The home side have lost their last 4 league games and concede 2.51 expected goals a game. Cambuur arrive unbeaten in 5, a run that includes a 2-2 with AZ Alkmaar last weekend. Even so, at home, the market makes Willem II narrow favourites at 38.1%, with Cambuur almost level at 36.6%. The total line is 3.25 goals, with the over at 47.5% — the market expects an open game between two sides it sees as close to equal.
read: Willem II host Cambuur bottom of the Eredivisie, two days after sacking John Stegeman and hours after naming 71-year-old Adrie Koster as interim coach, still without a win in nine league games. Cambuur arrive unbeaten in five and the market makes it near even — Willem II 38.1%, Cambuur 36.6% — with the level-ball handicap at zero and a total line of 3.25 goals.

facts.fact: Willem II sacked head coach John Stegeman with the club bottom of the Eredivisie on two points from nine games.
facts.meaning: The bottom club goes into this game in the middle of a coaching change, with the staff that prepared the season gone.

facts.fact: Willem II appointed 71-year-old Adrie Koster as interim head coach until a permanent replacement is found.
facts.meaning: A caretaker with limited time takes charge of a side that has not won all season, days before kick-off.

facts.fact: Willem II have lost their last four Eredivisie matches, the run reading LLLLD.
facts.meaning: The home side arrives on the worst run in the league, with the draw coming back on 11 September.

facts.fact: Cambuur are unbeaten in five Eredivisie matches, form DWDWD, with two wins and three draws.
facts.meaning: The visitors are the side in rhythm — hard to beat, if not prolific winners.

facts.fact: The market makes Willem II only fractional favourites at 38.1% to win, with Cambuur at 36.6%.
facts.meaning: Home advantage is worth almost nothing here: this is a near coin-flip between the bottom club and a mid-table visitor.

facts.fact: On the level-ball handicap, Willem II's price has fallen from 55.0% to 51.2% in recent days, with Cambuur's rising to 48.8%.
facts.meaning: The market has shifted toward Cambuur and now sees the two teams as virtually equal on neutral ground.

facts.fact: Cambuur drew 2-2 at home with AZ Alkmaar last weekend, a result Dutch media describe as a strong performance.
facts.meaning: The visitors come in off a point against one of the league's stronger sides, not off a scrappy win.

facts.fact: Willem II have conceded chances worth 2.51 xG per game across their last five matches.
facts.meaning: The defensive problem runs deeper than results: opponents are creating clear chances almost every week, including 3.65 xG at Sparta last Friday.

sources.fact: Willem II sacked head coach John Stegeman after nine Eredivisie matches without a win and only two points.
Willem II appointed 71-year-old Adrie Koster as interim head coach until a permanent replacement is found.
Koster will be assisted by Danny Schenkel and Pim Hendrix, and he steps back once a new head coach is hired.
Koster described the interim job as "quite a challenge" ("Het is wel een uitdaginkje").
Assistant coach Pascal Diender was dismissed along with Stegeman.
Willem II go into the Cambuur match bottom of the Eredivisie.
Cambuur held AZ to a 2-2 draw at home last weekend, a result Dutch media describe as a strong performance.
Cambuur went into the AZ match on the back of a 1-0 win over PEC Zwolle.
